utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]. Yes, Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case today.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is Case Number IT-02-60-A, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, I welcome you all to this second Status Conference. I would like to begin by checking in the usual way that the equipment is functioning. Gentlemen, can you hear me, Mr. Jokic and Mr. Blagojevic? THE APPELLANT JOKIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can hear you. THE APPELLANT BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: All the counsel can also hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can't hear either. Maybe it's this location, or maybe I've forgotten how to work the machinery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Sinatra, if it's any comfort, I have to learn back the whole process anew every time I take my seat. Now then, may we have the appearances. There are three appeals: Mr. Blagojevic first. Who is appearing for Mr. Blagojevic? The last time it was Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't wish to speak for Mr. Domazet, but he is not being able to hear the interpretation and he can't understand what you're saying at the moment. He does speak English, but he prefers to have the French interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Is there a problem, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: You have requested help. Help is coming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Can we await the technician? He is coming, I am told.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Test, test. This is a test.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Domazet, we were on the item relating to appearances. Ms. Sinatra volunteered the announcement that you were still appearing for Mr. Blagojevic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Yes, that's quite right. My name is Vladimir Domazet, I am appearing on behalf of Mr. Blagojevic, Vidoje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, you are appearing for Mr. Jokic?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but I have a gigantic staff that is only making this one appearance. We are minus Mr. Staker now, but we have Ms. Chrissa Loukas as co-counsel. We have Alfredo Strippoli as our legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And we have Ms. Aurora Bewicke as our intern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Ms. Aurora Bewicke, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And I'm Cynthia Sinatra, for Mr. Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Prosecution. Who is appearing for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon to my learned colleagues. Norman Farrell, Mr. Milbert Shin, and Janet Stewart appearing for the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: My first duty is to express to Ms. Sinatra the deepest sympathy of the Court on a recent mishap to her daughter, and we hope that that is now passed and that we can look to the future.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, this is the second Status Conference. The first one was held, I believe, on the 17th of June. As we know, there are two main purposes of a Status Conference. They are suggested by Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal. And the object is to allow the appellants to express concerns relating to the appeal and the detention conditions, and also to update the appellants with respect to the status of the case. Now, I will begin by noting, as I have said, that there are three appeals. First, an appeal by Mr. Jokic; second, an appeal by Mr. Blagojevic; and third, an appeal by the Prosecution. Perhaps I should begin by noting that in the appeal by the Prosecution the pleading process is practically complete. The Prosecution filed its reply brief on the 5th of July. What happened was that thereafter the Prosecution was granted leave to amend its notice of appeal and Mr. Blagojevic was also permitted to file additional submissions. He did so and requested time. Then the Prosecution sought to strike out some part of his additional submissions, and that has resulted in the present situation, which is that we are awaiting Mr. Blagojevic's response to the motion to strike out the additional submissions, the Prosecution's motion to strike out additional submissions of Mr. Blagojevic, and we hope to have his response to the Prosecution's motion I think today. Is that right? Then it will be for the Appeals Chamber to decide on the motion in the normal way. Then we have a second cause for delay. This is that Mr. Blagojevic has filed on the 19th of September a motion for an extension of time. Yesterday the Prosecution filed a response to this motion, opposing the suggested extension. Mr. Blagojevic is to reply on Monday coming. So thereafter we will deal with that motion as quickly as possible. And the third reason for some delay in the appeal process is this, that Mr. Jokic has on his part filed a request to amend his notice of appeal. He filed that on the 6th of September. The Prosecution filed its response to that request to amend the notice of appeal on the 16th of September, and this will also be considered by the Appeals Chamber in its full formation. I can't say that this appeal is the stalest that I've seen. The judgement was rendered in January this year. It is too early, I think - the pleading process has not run its full course - too early to prognosticate as to when the appeals might be heard. All I can say is they will be heard as soon as possible after the pleading process is over. For now, all I can do is to invite the parties to adhere as closely as they can to the pleading procedures prescribed by the Rules so that this matter would be heard eventually as soon as possible. Now, if there are any comments on that or on the conditions of detention of the appellants, counsel will let me know. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, as far as the conditions of detention are, I think Mr. Jokic has no problems with his detention at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's the same for Mr. Blagojevic with regard to his detention. But there are other matters that we might raise. May I -- may I raise these matters now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Of course. The only thing that I may point out is that on the last occasion we had a full discussion of the Drina Corps collection and related matters, and I think the transcripts on that occasion ran to some 32 pages, which is quite substantial for a sitting of this kind. I hope we don't repeat that, but do go ahead by all means, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, I will not raise the matter of the Drina collection, Drina Corps collection. I would like to raise other matters, other problems, related to the situation of my client. I checked all the transcripts related to the judgement, but I'm Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. faced with a major problem. As for the Status Conference of 27 March 2003, there was a closed session announced by Judge Schomburg during that status conference, Judge Schomburg being the Presiding Judge at the conference at that time, but the problem is that we do not have a transcript of this session, and according to what my client told me, this hearing is very important. He therefore insists that this transcript be uncovered but I was not able to access this transcript. It's page 201 where the open part of the Status Conference comes to an end and then Judge Schomburg announces that ten minutes later the hearing will resume in closed session. But although Mr. Blagojevic told me that he remembers perfectly that that hearing took place, we don't have -- find any transcripts. And the next page in the case of 200 -- page 202 is from the 5th of May, 2003, and that is to say the next pre-trial conference. Therefore, I'm not in a position to find out what happened with that particular transcript. And since it's one of our grounds of appeal, well, the situation is that I'm not in a position to find this transcript. [In English] One other thing. I should like to -- if we can go to closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, then we resume in open session. That is said for the record. Will there be any other intervention by counsel for the appellants?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I just wanted to express my appreciation for Mr. Farrell, the Prosecution's, and the Chamber's compassion during the incident where my daughter has broken her back. And as we speak, Your Honour, hurricane Rita, the eye is going to go over my home tonight at midnight, so I feel like Charlie Brown with a little cloud walking over my head. But we just have a few matters to address. One is that Mr. Farrell has handed us a gigantic index relating to the EDS system again, and Mr. Farrell has also stated that this index, of course, is not complete and can't be relied upon. But I covered this issue, I think pretty extensively, during the last Status Conference, and the person who has been working with the EDS system is my legal assistant, Mr. Strippoli, and if the court will indulge us, may Mr. Strippoli address the Court on this issue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRIPPOLI
utterances.text: Your Honour, this Defence is currently experiencing some difficulties in reviewing the documents made available Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to us by the Prosecution under the Drina Corps collection. These difficulties are due to the fact that the EDS system allows the user to carry out targeted searches within the collection, but doesn't allow to carry out a comprehensive and systemic review of all the documents contained in the collection. We appreciate the steps taken by the Prosecution in particular to make this list, this index, available to us and to make also some translated documents available to us. I would like to underline that these translated documents constitute just a minimum part of the documents present in the collection. We're talking about 115 out of almost 2.000 documents. In any case, and since most of the documents are not translated and no one in our Defence team understands B/C/S, we would like to be in a position to have Mr. Jokic review each and every document contained in the Drina Corps collection so that he can indicate to counsel which ones he thinks are relevant to his case. And in order to be in a position to do so, we would like to kindly ask the Prosecution to make all the documents contained in the Drina Corps collection available to us on a CD-ROM that we can deliver to the UNDU so that Mr. Jokic can review them. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Any difficulties with that request, Mr. Farrell?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: There may be, Your Honour. But if I can respond first to some of the other comments on the record. Ms. Sinatra's comments that we have filed an index that's not complete and cannot be relied upon, if that's the case, I'm happy to take it back, actually, and if they'd like to give it to me after this session, I'd be happy to receive it, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: You weren't suggesting that, were you?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I have offended Mr. Farrell in any way, I would like to apologise, because in his status report he says that I have offended him in some manner. I really think that I am just asking for disclosure of materials, that I would like to offer this to

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: The war map that we have been discussing, you have done everything in your power to abide by our request and I really appreciate it. The fact that neither one of us have understood exactly what the war map is makes it impossible to proceed on that issue, and I thank you for your cooperation. And if I have offended you in any way in any of my motions or any of my requests, please accept my humble apology.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: You have the gracious apology before you, Mr. Farrell. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Well, certainly the Prosecution appreciates the kind words of Ms. Sinatra, but it's the allegation of violation of Rule 68 when the document was in the possession of the Defence that we take issue with, not the specific matter of whether or not I am in any way personally offended. I take no issue with that. With respect to the index, as I think is evident from the status report, it doesn't list comprehensively every single word or every single explanation of what the documents are; it's an attempt to provide an identifier from which they can do further reviews. In relation to the other comments by Mr. Strippoli, the fact that there is only a minimal part of the documents translated, once again I don't think there is any insinuation, but there is certainly no obligation on the Prosecution to translate documents for the Defence. They, like the Prosecution, have to review the documents in B/C/S and there are language assistants available to the Defence through OLAD who can review them as well as we do with our language assistants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: What do you say about Mr. Strippoli's suggestion that the material might be handed over to his client?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to take a look at that and, if you don't mind, respond in writing to that request. I would like to determine what the practice and procedure is, what the impact is as to whether or not this can be done, because every other, I'm sure, appellant or accused may ask for the same. I don't know whether it's possible specifically, and I also am not sure what the obligations are of the Prosecution under Rule 68(ii). If it is possible and if we can do it without much difficulty, I will look into doing it, but I would like to make it clear that the Prosecution is not -- it's not the Prosecution's intention to provide CD-ROMs and material which have met the disclosure obligation under 68(ii). The requirement is it's made accessible to the Defence. They, like the Prosecution, can use a language assistant to review it and bring it to the attention of their client. But I certainly will, in this case, attempt to see if we can provide some assistance, though I am not, at this point in time, in a position to say whether we will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Will you be in a position to disclose your ultimate situation to Ms. Sinatra within, say, a stated time?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: I think we can probably do it by next week sometime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: What about that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, of course I didn't want to ask for an extension of time, and I believe that the Drina Corps collection does fall within the Rule 115 and not the evidence that was presented at trial, so as soon as they can provide it to us, we would most happily receive it. I also want to say that Mr. Farrell keeps referring to the fact that we can have translation assistants, interpretation assistants. The Defence does not have an on-staff interpreter. We rely on our applications to the CLSS department at the Tribunal to interpret and translate for us, and we have even applied for the CLSS to interpret our rough draft of our appeal brief -- translate it, excuse me -- so that we can go over it with Mr. Jokic, and they refuse. We cannot get any translations through the CLSS department. So we really have -- we are at the mercy of the Prosecution. When they have things translated, if we're allowed to have them, then that's the only way we have to review these documents and any and all collections that are in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, you're raising now a translation problem --

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: -- in addition to the problems you originally raise, which concern the convenient use by you of the index of material which Mr. Farrell has given to you. I don't know what is my reaction to your translation problems. Would you want thousands of pages translated?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I think what Mr. Strippoli and I are both asking for is we be given the Drina Corps collection on CD. Then Mr. Jokic, who speaks B/C/S and knows what documents would be relevant to his Defence, can tell us. And then at that point we can try to get CLSS to translate those documents for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Farrell says within a week he should be able to tell you of his definitive position on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: That's more than acceptable. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, then, will there be any other representations by either side of the aisle?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'd like to raise two matters. You stated with regard to the motion for extension of time that I can respond to the motion of the Prosecutor by Monday, and I will do so. I will file my response. But I'm faced with other difficulties. You said that you were expecting my response to the other motion of the Prosecutor today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, because of the problems I'm faced with with the -- because for the time being I do not have a legal assistant and I have not received the decision of the Registry as yet with regard to a new assistant being assigned to me, and since I'm always here and there, I was wondering, if at all possible, if I would be allowed to file that response on Monday as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Instead of today?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Farrell, do you have any objections to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: None whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, that is agreed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Okay. Any other remarks? Thank you. I would then take the adjournment and thank you all for coming and for participating in this very useful session. Thank you.
